description: The figure illustrates five schematic bar-chart shapes labeled “Increasing,” “Uniform,” “Decreasing,” “Spindle,” and “Bottleneck,” intended to represent different layer-wise allocation patterns. In each mini-chart, the horizontal axis contains the category label (the pattern name) centered beneath the bars, and there are no explicit tick marks, numeric scales, or axis titles; the vertical axis is implicit with no labeled units or tick intervals. For “Increasing,” five light-gray bars with black outlines rise from left to right, starting with a very short first bar and ending with the tallest fifth bar (approximately progressing from ~1 to ~5 in relative height). For “Uniform,” five bars of equal height are shown, all at the same mid-level (approximately ~4 in relative height). For “Decreasing,” five bars descend from left to right, with the first bar tallest and the fifth bar shortest (approximately ~5 down to ~1). For “Spindle,” five bars form a symmetric profile with short outer bars, taller middle bars, and the two central bars appearing equal and highest (approximately ~1, ~4, ~4, ~1 with a small fifth bar also short, giving a peaked middle). For “Bottleneck,” five bars show taller bars at the ends and shorter bars in the middle, with the first and fifth bars high and the three middle bars lower and roughly similar (approximately ~4, ~2, ~2, ~2, ~4). No legend is present, all bars share the same fill and outline styling, and there are no annotations or emphasized bars beyond the pattern labels.
